page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable tradeoff; stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with small-block cached read bandwidth showing average speeds, whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak, landing in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core execution, this instance is suited for workloads that do not require massive parallelization but benefit from high single-threaded throughput, such as text processing, basic software compilation, and static web serving. For machine learning, it handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds but exhibits poor prompt processing performance on medium 7B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware delivers solid compute density for standard general-purpose tasks, though workloads requiring high uncached memory bandwidth or heavy multi-threaded scaling may experience resource bottlenecks.
